correctness.rationale: Unique hierarchy and lattice registration give the exact phase identity (I-R)alpha=t for every Euclidean symmetry. Smith normal forms of the 23 nonidentity proper cubic rotations yield the one-dimensional 2-adic compatible sets, while explicit subgroup generators and a finite cubic-group census verify that every noncyclic point group forces an ordinary integral phase. Translation covariance then forces every invariant phase distribution to be Haar.

originality.rationale: The Chair44 source proves the order-24 symmetry bound and constructs the coherent 2-adic hierarchy phase, but targeted searches found no individual-stabilizer phase obstruction, no exact dimension-one exceptional phase set, and no noncyclic-implies-integral or zero-phase reduction. Searches of the current SCOPE archive found no overlapping record.

value.rationale: The result turns the source paper's open symmetry classification into an arithmetic phase sieve: generic phases forbid all symmetry, nonintegral phases allow only cyclic groups of order at most four, and every larger or noncyclic symmetry is confined up to translation to the zero-phase fiber.
